title: Worked example: drone weather in ATAK
breadcrumb: Worked example: drone weather in ATAK

blocks.html:
⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. The opendefense-platform is under breaking development; verify against the code before relying on details.

This page walks the chapter's demonstrator end to end: external weather data flowing into the deployed TAK server and rendering natively in ATAK — no plugin, no fork, stdlib Python only. The result is a translucent go/no-go heatmap on the real 1 km MGRS grid, hourly planning-step layers, tap-any-square point forecasts, and ETA-aware route weather. The mechanics behind each stage have their own pages in this chapter — ATAK import behaviours, Publishing with the Marti API, Importing a data source programmatically, and Defining standard data sources — this page just runs the whole distance once so you can see the shape of it. Full source: scripts/dronewx on branch feat/dronewx-demo.

What it is

A 1 km go/no-go heatmap for a light quadcopter (<2 kg class) over a 24×24 km AOI around Helsinki — 576 cells, one forecast point per cell, refreshed on a cron. Each cell is a real 1 km MGRS square: cell edges sit on whole-km UTM eastings/northings, so the grid matches what ATAK's own coordinate display calls 35V LG 84 72. The WGS84↔UTM conversion (Krueger series) plus the MGRS 100 km letter scheme is ~60 lines of stdlib math in dronewx.py — no pyproj, no GDAL, no PIL.

Banding is deliberately crude — three gust thresholds and two weather bumps, not a flight-physics model: green <8, yellow <12, orange <16, red ≥16 m/s gust; bumped one band by rain >0.5 mm/h or temperature <−10 °C, straight to red by rain >4 mm/h or <−20 °C. It is a placeholder on purpose — see Swapping in real data.

The pipeline

Four small pieces, each replaceable on its own:

flowchart LR om["Open-Meteo
MET Nordic, 1 km native"] dw["dronewx.py
fetch_grid() + band()"] cells["cells.kmz
576 tappable polygons"] rast["gust_h00/03/06/12.kmz
one GroundOverlay each"] pkg["package.py
dronewx-pkg.zip"] up["upload.sh
3 Marti calls"] tak["TAK mission dronewx"] atak["ATAK
Available Packages"] om --> dw dw --> cells --> pkg dw --> rast --> pkg pkg --> up --> tak --> atak

blocks.html:
Fetch. fetch_grid() asks Open-Meteo for models=metno_nordic (MET Nordic — 1 km native resolution over Fennoscandia, so one point per km square is honest sampling, not interpolation theatre), batched ≤96 coordinates per request — more and the URI blows past the length cap with an HTTP 414.

Build. The output is deliberately split: cells.kmz carries only vector polygons, gust_hXX.kmz carries exactly one GroundOverlay each. This is the GRG trap: a KMZ mixing multiple GroundOverlays and Placemarks imports as a GRG (georeferenced graphic) — rasters mosaicked into one image, every placemark silently dropped. Each raster pixel is mapped lat/lon → UTM → cell, so the axis-aligned PNG still lands exactly on the MGRS grid. The polygons carry no IconStyle or LabelStyle at all — include either (even at scale 0) and every cell grows a white centre dot.

Package. package.py wraps everything in one Mission Package: MANIFEST/manifest.xml (MissionPackageManifest v2, onReceiveImport=true, uid a stable uuid5 so every refresh is the same package). This step is not optional — upload a raw KMZ as a server package and ATAK unzips it file-by-file and asks the operator to "Select a location on the map to place: h00.png".

Publish. upload.sh pulls the tak-server-admin client certificate straight from the cluster Secret (namespace app-tak) and makes three Marti REST calls:

HASH="$(shasum -a 256 "$FILE" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
# 1. create the mission — 201 first time, 409 after, both fine
curl ... -X PUT "https://$HOST:8443/Marti/api/missions/dronewx?creatorUid=dronewx&defaultRole=MISSION_SUBSCRIBER"
# 2. upload to Enterprise Sync — dedupes on hash
curl ... -F "assetfile=@$FILE" "https://$HOST:8443/Marti/sync/missionupload?hash=$HASH&filename=$FILE&creatorUid=dronewx"
# 3. attach to the mission
curl ... -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"hashes\":[\"$HASH\"]}" \
  "https://$HOST:8443/Marti/api/missions/dronewx/contents?creatorUid=dronewx"

The whole thing is idempotent, so it doubles as the refresh path. Note that every missionupload is listed as Tool: public in /Marti/sync/search — clients see it under Available Packages even without subscribing to the mission.

Pull. On an enrolled ATAK client (see Enrolling: getting a client certificate): Data Packages tool → download icon → pick the server → dronewx-pkg.zip → Download. Files land as atak/overlays/cells.kmz and atak/grg/gust_h*.kmz — verified on ATAK-CIV 5.7.0.6 against TAK Server 5.8.69-RELEASE.

What the operator sees

blocks.alt: the go/no-go grid aligned to the MGRS kilometer grid

blocks.html: The package imports as one overlay group — cells.kmz plus the hour rasters, each with its own eye toggle. The fills are translucent by design so the basemap stays readable underneath.

blocks.alt: tap deconfliction lists squares by MGRS reference

blocks.html: Tapping where several polygons fall within tap radius opens ATAK's deconfliction list — each entry is the cell's MGRS reference, which is the whole point of aligning the grid: the operator reads 35V LG 82 68 off the list and it is the square on their map.

blocks.alt: a square's hourly forecast in Details

blocks.html: Radial menu → bottom icon opens Details: plain-text hourly rows — 00:00Z gust 11 wind 5 ↑ RH 95% 17C rain 2.0 [orange].

blocks.alt: the full 24 h table under METADATA, route corridor visible behind

blocks.html: The full 24 h table is readable under METADATA. This is the hourly lookup mechanism — a tap, not a slider.
The planning steps (+00h/+03h/+06h/+12h) are four separate rasters, individually toggleable in Overlay Manager.

blocks.alt: the wide view over the Helsinki region

blocks.html:
Route weather

routewx.py closes the loop: plan a route in ATAK, export it as KML, then

python3 routewx.py route.kml 2026-08-31T16:00+00:00 12
# routewx.kmz: 4 legs, 13.5 km, 19 min, takeoff 16:00Z, worst band: orange

Each leg gets its ETA from cumulative distance / speed and samples the same forecast at that hour — the weather you will actually meet, not the weather right now. Legs render as wide colored LineStrings; each carries ETA 16:04Z (fc 16:00Z): gust 10 m/s, wind 6 m/s ↗, RH 96%, 18 C, rain 0.0 mm. One caveat: the topmost fill wins the tap, so to tap a corridor leg under the weather cells, hide the cells layer first.

Swapping in real data

A collaborator replaces exactly two functions in dronewx.py and keeps everything else:

  • **fetch_grid()** — must return one dict per cell centre (row-major over the grid) with hourly arrays under ["hourly"][<variable>][h] for the six variables the pipeline reads (gust, wind speed/direction, humidity, temperature, precipitation). Where the numbers come from is your business.
  • **band()** — the airframe envelope:

def band(gust, precip=0.0, temp=15.0):
    """Go/no-go band for a <2 kg quadcopter."""
    i = (gust >= 8) + (gust >= 12) + (gust >= 16)   # wind is the primary factor
    if precip > 4 or temp < -20:
        i = 3
    elif precip > 0.5 or temp < -10:
        i = min(i + 1, 3)
    return BANDS[i]

Anything that maps a cell-hour to green/yellow/orange/red works. The grid geometry, KMZ writers, packaging and publishing don't care. The refresh loop is a plain cron — idempotency in upload.sh makes re-publishing free:

*/30 * * * *  cd .../scripts/dronewx && python3 dronewx.py \
  && python3 package.py cells.kmz gust_h*.kmz && ./upload.sh dronewx-pkg.zip

Honest rough edges

  • No time slider. Core ATAK has no timeline/playback at all (verified against the full feature list; KML TimeSpan changes nothing). Hour steps are separate toggleable layers plus the per-cell table — native, but not an animation.
  • HTML is stripped from KML descriptions in Details — a <table> collapses to a run-on string. The "table" you see is plain text joined with <br/>, the only markup that survives.
  • API-created inputs are not persisted. If you extend this to streaming CoT, /Marti/api/inputs POSTs are gone on pod restart — re-POST each run (a 500 "Input name already exists" is fine). See Pushing data to TAK Server.
  • TAK is slow after a restart — the Marti API takes minutes to come up after the tak-server pod (namespace app-tak) restarts, and takrmapi client-zip requests 500 with a TimeoutError until it does. Don't debug your script during that window.
